config.title: Build file upload preview and progress UI

intro.title: Build file upload preview and progress UI
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web interface that allows users to select an image file and see a preview of it before uploading. You'll learn how to use the FileReader API to read file data and display it as an image. The core programming concept is handling user input events and updating the DOM dynamically based on file selection. You'll work with HTML input elements, event listeners, and JavaScript to create a responsive UI that shows the selected image and a simulated upload progress bar.
intro.usecase: File upload previews with progress indicators are essential in modern web applications where users need visual feedback during file operations. You'll see this pattern in social media platforms like Facebook or Instagram when uploading photos, where thumbnails appear immediately with upload progress bars. Cloud storage services like Google Drive or Dropbox use similar interfaces to show file previews and upload status during document transfers. E-commerce sites implement this for product image uploads in admin dashboards, allowing merchants to verify images before final submission. Even in productivity tools like project management software, teams upload attachments with previews to ensure correct files are shared.

objectives: Initialize a file input element to accept user file selections
Configure an event listener to capture file selection changes
Implement file preview generation using the FileReader API
Construct a progress bar UI element to display upload status
Update the progress bar dynamically during simulated file upload
Bind event handlers to manage file upload lifecycle events
Render selected file metadata (name, size, type) in the UI

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main FileUpload component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named FileUpload that returns an empty fragment for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called FileUpload that returns React.Fragment (<> </>) or a simple div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the FileUpload component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a FileUpload component function that returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A FileUpload component function is defined and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main FileUpload component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named FileUpload that returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a function called FileUpload that returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize state for selected file
steps.instruction: Inside the FileUpload component, add a useState hook to store the selected file. Initialize it with null.
steps.hint: Call useState with null as the initial value and destructure the returned array into a state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a user object
const [user, setUser] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable (e.g., selectedFile) initialized to null, ready to store a file object when selected.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with null and destructured into a state variable and setter function inside the component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useState with null and destructuring the array into two variables.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the useState hook inside the component with null as the initial value.

steps.title: Initialize state for upload progress
steps.instruction: Inside your FileUpload component, add another useState hook to store upload progress, initializing it as 0.
steps.hint: You'll need to call useState again with an initial value of 0 and destructure the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: another state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: selectedFile and uploadProgress, with uploadProgress initialized to 0.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call with initial value 0, destructured into a state variable (e.g., uploadProgress) and setter function (e.g., setUploadProgress).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've properly initialized the state with 0 and destructured both the state variable and setter function.
steps.feedbackWrong: add another useState hook inside the component to store upload progress, starting at 0.

steps.title: Create file selection handler
steps.instruction: Inside your FileUpload component, create a function named handleFileChange that takes an event parameter and updates the selectedFile state with the first file from event.target.files.
steps.hint: Define the function before the return statement. Use setSelectedFile to update the state with event.target.files[0].
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleFileChange function that updates selectedFile state when called with a file input event.
successCriteria: A handleFileChange function is defined that takes an event parameter and calls setSelectedFile with event.target.files[0].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your handleFileChange function takes an event parameter and calls setSelectedFile with the first file from event.target.files.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named handleFileChange that updates the selectedFile state with the selected file from an input event.

steps.title: Create upload simulation handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleUpload inside your component that will simulate file upload progress using setInterval.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses setInterval to increment the uploadProgress state from 0 to 100 over time.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleUpload function is defined inside the component, ready to simulate progress updates.
successCriteria: The handleUpload function is defined and uses setInterval to increment uploadProgress.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it uses setInterval to increment the progress state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleUpload function isn't properly defined yet. Create a function that simulates upload progress.

steps.title: Add file input element
steps.instruction: In the return statement of your FileUpload component, add a file input element with type='file' and wire its onChange event to the handleFileChange handler.
steps.hint: Use the <input> tag with type='file'. Set its onChange prop to call your handleFileChange function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: adding a file input
<input type="file" onChange={handleFileSelection} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now renders a file input that will trigger your handleFileChange function when a file is selected.
successCriteria: File input element is present with type='file'
onChange event is wired to handleFileChange
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both the file input element and wired its onChange event to handleFileChange.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file input element or its onChange handler is missing. Check that you've added <input type="file" onChange={handleFileChange} />.

steps.title: Add upload button
steps.instruction: Add a button element after the file input and wire its onClick event to the handleUpload handler.
steps.hint: Place the button inside the div, after the input element. Use the onClick attribute to call handleUpload.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with an event handler
<button onClick={handleAction}>Start Action</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Upload' appears after the file input, and clicking it will trigger the upload simulation.
successCriteria: A button element is added after the file input with onClick={handleUpload}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it's placed after the input and has onClick={handleUpload}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not correctly wired. Add a button after the input with onClick={handleUpload}.

steps.title: Display selected file preview
steps.instruction: Add conditional rendering inside your component's return statement to display the selected file's name and size when selectedFile is not null.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator or logical && to conditionally render JSX based on whether selectedFile exists. Access the file's name and size properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: When a file is selected, the UI will display its name and size below the file input.
successCriteria: The component conditionally renders file information (name and size) only when selectedFile is not null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying both the file name and size when selectedFile exists.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using conditional rendering (like a ternary or logical &&) and accessing selectedFile.name and selectedFile.size.

steps.title: Add progress bar display
steps.instruction: Add a progress bar element that shows the current upload progress percentage, and conditionally render it only when progress is greater than 0.
steps.hint: You can use a <div> with a width style based on the uploadProgress state, and wrap it in a conditional check.
steps.expectedOutcome: A progress bar appears during upload simulation, showing the current progress percentage, and disappears when upload is complete or not started.
successCriteria: Progress bar element is added with conditional rendering based on uploadProgress > 0, and displays the progress percentage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some progress display, but make sure it conditionally renders only when progress > 0 and shows the percentage value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The progress bar isn't working as expected. Check that you're using the uploadProgress state and conditionally rendering based on its value.
